h1: China visa-free travel for British citizens: what you need to know
title: China Visa-Free for British Citizens Until 31 Dec 2026 | UVS
description: British citizens can visit China visa-free for up to 30 days until 31 December 2026. Here is who qualifies, what it covers and when you still need a visa.
intro: Since 17 February 2026, British passport holders can visit mainland China without a visa for up to 30 days. China visa-free entry is a big change for UK travellers, but it has limits, and it is currently due to end on 31 December 2026.

sections.heading: What does China visa-free entry cover?
sections.text:
Holders of ordinary British passports can enter mainland China without a visa for up to 30 days for:
- Business, including meetings and trade fairs
- Tourism
- Visiting family and friends
- Exchanges
- Transit

sections.heading: When do you still need a China visa?
sections.text:
You still need a visa if you:
- Plan to stay longer than 30 days on a single visit
- Are going to work, study or report as a journalist
- Are travelling on a passport that isn't covered, for example if you live in the UK on an Indian, Pakistani or Nigerian passport
- Are travelling after 31 December 2026 and the policy hasn't been extended

sections.heading: Not a British passport holder? You may still need a visa
sections.text:
China visa-free entry depends on the passport you hold, not where you live. Living in the UK on a visa, Indefinite Leave to Remain or settled status does not give you visa-free entry to China.

You will need a visa before you travel if you hold a passport from, for example:
- India
- Pakistan (an invitation letter from China is required, see below)
- Nigeria (an invitation letter from China is required, see below)
- Bangladesh
- Sri Lanka
- Ghana
- The Philippines

Pakistani and Nigerian passport holders: your application must include an invitation letter from a company, organisation or host in China. Without it, the visa centre will not accept your application. We can tell you exactly what the letter needs to say before you ask your host for it.

Many EU passport holders, including French, German, Italian, Spanish and Polish nationals, can also enter China visa-free for up to 30 days. Check your nationality before you book.

To apply from the UK as a non-British national, you will usually need:
- Your passport, valid for at least six months, with blank pages
- Proof of UK residence, such as your eVisa share code, BRP or ILR
- Flight and hotel bookings, or an invitation letter, depending on the visa type
- An invitation letter from China if you hold a Pakistani or Nigerian passport

We prepare China visa applications for UK residents of all nationalities, including Pakistani and Nigerian passport holders, and check every document before it is submitted. [Start your China visa application](/china-visa-application/) or see our [China business visa](/china-business-visa/) page.

sections.heading: Planning trips for 2027
sections.text: The China visa-free policy for British citizens currently runs until 31 December 2026. China has extended similar policies before, but there is no guarantee, and in mid-November 2026 China's Foreign Ministry had not confirmed whether it will be extended. If you're planning a trip for early 2027, check the latest position before you book, and allow time to apply for a visa if you need one. We will update this page as soon as China confirms. For more detail, read [China visa-free 2027: will UK travellers still need a visa?](/blog/china-visa-free-2027/)

sections.heading: How we can help
sections.text: We arrange Chinese visas for UK residents who need them, including business (M), tourist (L), family (Q and S), work (Z) and student (X) visas. Our online China visa form reads your passport details automatically and lists exactly which documents your visa type needs.

sections.heading: What to carry when you travel
sections.text: Even without a visa, take your passport (valid for at least six months), your return or onward ticket, and details of where you’re staying. Border officers can ask to see them. If you plan to work, study or stay longer than 30 days, you still need a visa.

faqs.q: Do British citizens need a visa for China?
faqs.a: Not for visits of up to 30 days for tourism, business, family visits, exchanges or transit, until 31 December 2026.

faqs.q: Can I work in China on visa-free entry?
faqs.a: No. Working in China needs a Z visa and a work permit.

faqs.q: Is China visa-free entry for British citizens permanent?
faqs.a: No. It’s currently due to end on 31 December 2026. Check before you plan trips for 2027.

faqs.q: I live in the UK but don't have a British passport. Can I enter China visa-free?
faqs.a: Only if your own passport is on China's visa-free list, for example many EU passports. UK residence or ILR does not count. Indian, Pakistani, Nigerian, Bangladeshi and many other passport holders need a visa, and Pakistani and Nigerian nationals also need an invitation letter from China.
